newsitem.title: USA: EMU won't change Europe's basic forex stance - Buba.
newsitem.headline: EMU won't change Europe's basic forex stance - Buba.

text.p: European foreign exchange rate policy is expected to remain broadly unchanged after the 1999 launch of monetary union and the establishment of a new central bank, a senior Bundesbank official said.

Bernd Goos, who heads the Bundesbank's International Relations Department, told a conference here he did not expect Europe to set up currency target zones with the dollar and the yen after the introduction of its new currency, the euro.
Goos played down fears that the euro's launch would disrupt Europe or the world economy.

"I fail to see any big bang or dramatic change," he said, arguing that European countries have been running a de facto monetary union for some time by linking their currencies through the Exchange Rate Mechanism.
He said that any increase in the euro's international role at the expense of the dollar will happen in a "gradual manner."
